stories.headline: Poland signs EU SAFE defence loan despite presidential veto, triggering political battle with Nawrocki
stories.summary: Poland became the first EU country to sign a loan agreement under the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) programme, securing up to €43.7 billion in preferential financing for military modernisation. Prime Minister Tusk called it a 'breakthrough moment' while repeatedly criticising President Nawrocki for vetoing the implementing legislation; opposition-aligned protestors gathered outside Tusk's private home in Sopot, and right-wing commentators called the signing illegal. Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz and Finance Minister Domański signed on Poland's behalf.

stories.headline: ABW publishes first public report in 12 years, warns of professionalised Russian sabotage networks and Chinese influence operations
stories.summary: Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) published its first public activity report since 2012, covering 2024-2025 and documenting over 60 espionage investigations, 82 charges, and an unprecedented shift in Russian tactics from disposable amateur recruits to professional sabotage networks. The report also detailed cyberattacks on five water treatment plants attributed to Russian-linked APT groups, growing Chinese intelligence activity targeting lobbying and media, and rising youth radicalisation. ABW chief Col. Rafał Syrysko gave concurrent media interviews.

stories.headline: NBP holds interest rates but Glapiński signals rate hikes increasingly probable amid inflation concerns
stories.summary: The Monetary Policy Council held Poland's reference rate at 3.75% in its May meeting, in line with expectations, but Governor Adam Glapiński delivered a markedly hawkish press conference warning that the probability of rate hikes had risen since April due to geopolitical energy price pressures. NBP also disclosed gold reserves reached 595 tonnes by end-April. A separate sub-story ran alongside: PM Tusk has withheld countersignature on Nawrocki's nomination of Kightley as NBP deputy governor for three months, leaving the post vacant.

stories.headline: Nawrocki proposes national referendum on EU climate policy, seen as PiS electoral strategy
stories.summary: President Nawrocki formally submitted a request to the Senate to hold a nationwide referendum asking Poles whether they support EU climate policy, which he blamed for rising energy costs. The coalition government and Senate leadership rejected the initiative, with senior government figures calling it propaganda and legally meaningless since Polish referendum results cannot override EU law. Multiple analysts described it as a PiS-coordinated campaign move ahead of 2027 elections, with PM candidate Przemysław Czarnek expected to carry the referendum message.

stories.headline: Nawrocki appoints new BBN chief Grodecki after Cenckiewicz resignation, raising conflict-of-interest questions
stories.summary: President Nawrocki named Bartosz Grodecki, a former Deputy Interior Minister, as the new head of the National Security Bureau, replacing Sławomir Cenckiewicz who resigned in April. The appointment drew immediate controversy because Grodecki had been an advisor to a defence-industry firm lobbying for legislation that Nawrocki himself had vetoed. Grodecki's inaugural statements signalled strong alignment with the presidency against the Tusk government, including on SAFE and the relocation of US troops.

stories.headline: Ziobro flees Hungary for United States, confirms he will fight extradition
stories.summary: Former Justice Minister Zbigniew Ziobro confirmed on Sunday that he had left Hungary — where he had enjoyed political asylum from Viktor Orbán — and travelled to the United States. Ziobro, who faces charges related to the Justice Fund scandal and up to 25 years in prison, announced he had joined TV Republika as a political commentator (on a journalist visa) and vowed to continue fighting PM Tusk politically. Justice Minister Żurek immediately announced extradition proceedings.

stories.headline: Mentzen detained at London airport for three hours, sparks free-speech debate and internal Confederation tensions
stories.summary: Confederation leader Sławomir Mentzen was held for over three hours at a London airport during passport control on a private family trip; British authorities told him an unidentified organisation had flagged him as a potential public speaker. Mentzen called the UK a 'totalitarian state' and thanked FM Sikorski for diplomatic intervention. Separately, his earlier description of Chief of Staff Gen. Wiesław Kukuła as 'abnormal' sparked a cross-party backlash and was linked to internal Confederation tensions, including the departure of MEP Zajączkowska-Hernik from his party.

stories.headline: ECHR orders Poland to allow newly elected Constitutional Tribunal judges to begin work; Tribunal president ignores ruling
stories.summary: The European Court of Human Rights issued an interim measure ordering Polish authorities to stop blocking four newly elected Constitutional Tribunal judges — chosen by the Sejm in March — from taking up their duties. CT president Bogdan Święczkowski refused to admit them, and his office stated the ECHR ruling did not apply to the CT's internal operations. PM Tusk commented 'Did it get through?' on social media. Legal experts described the impasse as a constitutional crisis.

stories.headline: ZondaCrypto scandal expands: Tusk pushes revised crypto bill after Nawrocki veto, links exchange to Russian mafia
stories.summary: Prime Minister Tusk announced emergency re-submission of a crypto-assets regulation bill to the Sejm in the immediate aftermath of President Nawrocki vetoing the original version, calling ZondaCrypto's collapse 'the biggest scandal in decades.' Tusk alleged ZondaCrypto had links to Russian organised crime and had financed right-wing politicians including Nawrocki's election campaign. Nawrocki simultaneously submitted a rival presidential crypto bill. The government and opposition traded accusations about which side was protecting illicit crypto interests.

stories.headline: Trump suggests US troops from Germany could relocate to Poland; Nawrocki welcomes it, Tusk more cautious
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly suggested that some of the ~5,000 US troops being withdrawn from Germany could be redeployed to Poland, praising Nawrocki as 'a great warrior' and saying 'Poland would want this.' President Nawrocki — including during a separate visit to Lithuania — enthusiastically declared Poland ready to host the troops. Prime Minister Tusk struck a more cautious tone, saying Poland should not 'poach' soldiers from allies, which drew criticism from Kaczyński and the opposition. New BBN chief Grodecki called Trump's statement 'absolutely breakthrough.'

stories.headline: Andrzej Poczobut freed from Belarusian prison in prisoner exchange, Trump and Nawrocki credited
stories.summary: Polish journalist Andrzej Poczobut was released from a Belarusian prison after over five years, as part of a 'five-for-five' prisoner exchange negotiated with Lukashenko. PM Tusk greeted Poczobut at the border; President Trump posted that the release followed Nawrocki's request to him in September 2025, attributing credit to both Nawrocki and himself. Polish intelligence services ABW and AW were also cited as playing key roles in the negotiations.

stories.headline: 193rd Smolensk monthly commemoration disrupted by counter-protesters; Kaczyński threatens future prosecutions
stories.summary: The 193rd monthly Smolensk commemoration took place in Warsaw's Piłsudski Square with Jarosław Kaczyński and a delegation of PiS politicians. The ceremony was again disrupted by counter-demonstrators, prompting Kaczyński to accuse them of being 'Russian agents' and to warn that 'honest courts will resolve this and these people will be somewhere else' — remarks interpreted as threats of future prosecution. A number of senior PiS figures were absent.
